config.description: Added after seeing the 1e results, motivated by the literature: de Chazal et al. (2004) classify beats with RR-interval features, and in 1e, where the model sees one beat without its own RR interval, S beats were almost never detected. 1e stays as reported; 1f does not replace it. Fixed before any 1f run: identical to 1e (the same DS1 / DS2 records dealt to the same hospitals per seed, seeds 0-2, 20 rounds x 2 local epochs, batch 32, learning rate 0.003, local only, FedAvg and pooled training, no FedProx or DP, the same evaluation, final round reported even if a curve peaks earlier), except that each beat also gets three RR-interval inputs from the reference annotations: pre-RR, post-RR and the local average RR over the 10 surrounding intervals, each divided by the record's own average RR (experiments/mitdb.py, rr_features). The model is the same CNN-BiLSTM with the three RR inputs concatenated to its mean-pooled BiLSTM output (after dropout) before the final linear layer, which grows from 128 to 131 inputs (CNN-BiLSTM+RR, used only by the experiment harness). The same training order as 1e (round ids named after 1e) and the same 5 PyTorch threads, so each seed is a paired comparison with the same seed of 1e; a check before the run reproduced 1e's seed 0, round 1 FedAvg score exactly. Simplification: dividing by the record's average RR uses beats that come after the current one (and post-RR uses the next beat); a deployed system would use a running average of past beats only.
config.title: 1f. Patient-wise with RR-interval inputs: ECG, PhysioNet MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database (DS1 / DS2)
